questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: The state of nature as a measuring rod
questions.learningObjective: Explain the role of the state of nature as a standard
questions.stem: A thinker treats the state of nature as a measuring rod for judging political authority and its limits.

options.text: It sets a baseline of natural equality against which claims of rule are tested.
It proves that every government begins from a written constitution.
options.misconception: confuses a hypothetical baseline with a documentary origin

options.text: It shows that rulers always act from pure self interest.
options.misconception: reduces a normative test to a cynical description

options.text: It replaces history with an abstract mathematical model.

questions.explanation: The state of nature works as a standard for measuring legitimate authority, not as a historical narrative or proof of constitutions. The tempting wrong ideas overread it as history, cynicism, or formalism.

questions.explanation: When a government spends the trust placed in it, the condition of obedience fails and resistance becomes justified. The wrong options treat power as self-justifying or transfer judgment elsewhere.
questions.hint: Consider what a trust implies about conditions.

questions.explanation: Toleration as a limit on the state need not imply full equality; it can permit worship while withholding office. The wrong options either inflate or invert what toleration demands.
